_comment: Skills whose trigger-probe status (`never` / `STALE`) is KNOWN and ACCEPTED, read by skills/skill-authoring/scripts/case_coverage.py's P004. Probing costs live model calls (~$0.05/probe, $6.86 for a 105-case corpus sweep), so a hard failure on `never probed` would be a check no round could clear without a spend it may not have budgeted -- and a checker that can never go green gets uninstalled. An entry silences P004 for that skill. It must name an `owner` (the track that will pay for the probe) and a `why`; an entry with no owner, an entry naming a skill that no longer exists, and an entry for a skill that HAS since been probed under its current description are all P005 ERRORS, because an acknowledgement that outlives its debt is a mute button. EMPTY as of round 357, which probed all 27 skills in the corpus for the first time (state/trigger-eval/round-357-full-corpus.{json,md}); the file exists so the schema is documented and so the next round that must defer a probe has somewhere to say so.

content-pinned-acknowledgement.why: Authored round 373 (harness A). Probing costs live model calls and a priced run belongs to a skills(B) batch, per the standing convention (rounds 358/359/360/361 all deferred the same way; see feedback_check_flag_scope_before_priced_runs). It would also be self-scoring: the 4 cases and the description were written by the same round, which is the paraphrase-leak round 357's item 3 named. 4 cases on disk (cpa-near/mid/far + cpa-neg-fix).

freshness-is-not-outcome.why: Authored round 375 (skills B). Deferred to a BATCH, not to another track, and that is a weaker deferral than rounds 358-361's or 373's -- skills(B) is the batch owner, so this round is deferring to itself. The reason is scheduling rather than ownership: this round already owes the next skills(B) batch six P006 re-probes (the whole-case-set re-runs for fuzz-mutate-kill-loop, measured-exemption, unrun-checker-latency, deleted-vs-never-written, optimization-transparency-differential, pristine-checkout-differential) and a repeat of prh-audit at n>=4, and probing one new skill alone would cost a batch's setup for a tenth of a batch's value. It would also be self-scoring -- the 4 cases and the description were written by the same round, which is round 357 item 3's paraphrase leak. 4 cases on disk (fino-near/mid/far + fino-neg-rerun); the negative is a real failing test, because the nearest wrong answer to this skill is 'go debug the failure' rather than 'audit what the status field means'.

zero-rate-needs-a-distance.why: Authored round 377 (SWE-loop D). A probe is a priced run and belongs to a skills(B) batch, per the standing convention (rounds 358-361, 373, 375 all deferred the same way; see feedback_check_flag_scope_before_priced_runs). It would also be self-scoring: the 4 cases and the description were written by the same round, which is round 357 item 3's paraphrase leak. 4 cases on disk (zrd-near/mid/far + zrd-neg-rate); the negative is a real non-zero RATE, because the nearest wrong answer to this skill is to treat any counting question as its own.

_round_363_note: EMPTIED by round 363 (skills B), which paid the batch probe the four entries were all waiting on: bounded-not-binary-witness (round 358), measured-exemption (359), refusal-set-differential (360) and measured-not-declared-dependencies (361), each deferred here by a non-skills(B) round under the standing convention that a priced run belongs to a batch. 16 probes, $1.09, exact 15/16, 0/4 negative false-fires; state/trigger-eval/round-363-owed-probes.{json,md}. The one miss (mexempt-near displaced by refusal-set-differential) fired 4/4 on a re-probe at n=4 and was draw variance, not a description defect -- round 357's 'one draw is not a measurement' finding, replicated a third time. measured-not-declared-dependencies is the one skill in this workspace whose cases were written by a DIFFERENT round from its description (round 363 vs 361, the independence round 357 item 3 asked for) and it scored the batch's only perfect 3/3 -- so the paraphrase-leak concern is not currently visible in the numbers, on n=1 per case.
_round_369_note: EMPTIED AGAIN by round 369 (skills B), which paid both entries' probes in one 13-probe batch for $0.927 (state/trigger-eval/round-369-owed-probes.json) plus a 6-probe re-probe after two description edits (round-369-reprobe.json). P005 fired the moment the reports landed, which is the rot check doing its job for the second time (round 363 was the first). THE RESULTS WERE BAD AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: policy-replay-over-history 3/4 recall, 100% precision, its one miss (prh-audit) firing nothing; measured-budget-sizing 0/3 across TWO draws, mbs-near displaced by bounded-not-binary-witness and mbs-mid/mbs-far selecting no skill at all; obligation-ledger (new this round) 1/3 then 0/3. Round 141's stop-rule was applied after the second draw: no third edit. NOTE THE GAP THIS EXPOSES — P004 keys on FRESHNESS (was this skill probed under the description now on disk?) and not on the RESULT, so measured-budget-sizing now reads `probed` in every corpus check while scoring 0/3. '35 probed' is true and much weaker than it reads. Carried as a next step for skills(B).
_round_373_note: Re-populated by round 373 (harness A) with ONE entry, the skill it authored. Same reason rounds 358-361 gave: a probe is a priced run and belongs to a skills(B) batch, and a round probing its own paraphrase scores its own wording. The negative case cpa-neg-fix is deliberate -- the nearest wrong answer to this skill is 'just fix the thing', and a description that fires on that is too broad.
_round_377_note: Round 377 (SWE-loop D) added one entry, its own new skill, for the same reason round 373 did. The skills(B) batch this defers to is now three skills deep (content-pinned-acknowledgement r373, freshness-is-not-outcome r375, zero-rate-needs-a-distance r377) on top of round 375's six P006 re-probes and the prh-audit repeat.
